thinking: I'm going to extract the data, run a holdout check on the lambda values at m=1024, fit the L1 model, and set up the L2 probe, all in one code run to save turns.

text: Layer-1 data is in. In one run: extract it, check held-out λ, fit layer 1 at m=1024, then set up the layer-2 probe.

input.code:
exec(open('seq.py').read())
L=1
extract_probe(L, 'pass_16', 2, 'B1'); extract_probe(L, 'pass_17', 2, 'B2')
A, S = all_data(L); te = (S<100) & (S%2==1)
def holdout(L, m, lam_rel, A, S, te):
    tr = ~te
    keep,B,mk,mt = fit_layer(L, m, lam_rel, A=A[tr], save=False)
    pre = f"roberta.encoder.layer.{L}."
    W1 = base(pre+"intermediate.dense.weight").astype(np.float64); b1 = base(pre+"intermediate.dense.bias")
    W2 = base(pre+"output.dense.weight").astype(np.float64)
    At = A[te].astype(np.float64); H = gelu(At@W1.T+b1); Y = H@W2.T; Z = At+Y
    drop = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(3072), keep)
    T = H[:,drop]@W2[:,drop].T; pred = (H[:,keep]-mk)@B + mt
    den = np.sqrt(((Z-Z.mean(0))**2).sum(1)).mean()
    return round(np.sqrt(((T-pred)**2).sum(1)).mean()/den,4), round(np.sqrt(((T-T.mean(0))**2).sum(1)).mean()/den,4)
print([(lr, holdout(L,1024,lr,A,S,te)) for lr in [0.3,0.1,0.03]])
restore_layer(L)
fit_layer(L, 1024, 0.05)
print(setup_probe(L+1, 1024)); print(load_keeps().keys())
